In this study, 98W-1.4Ni-0.6Fe (wt.%, 98W) mixed powder was prepared by a self-developed double laser-powder bed fusion (DL-PBF) system. The schematic diagram of DL-PBF process is illustrated in Fig. 1(a), with a dual laser interval distance of 0.2 mm. The entire preparation process was carried out in a forming chamber filled with argon (oxygen content: < 100 ppm). The laser powder, scanning speed, layer thickness and hatch spacing were set to 350W, 600 mm/s, 20 μm, and 0.1 mm, respectively. Both lasers operated under identical parameters.

Before that, the temperature was gradually increased from ambient conditions to 1350 ◦C for 1 h. This step is intended to form initial skeleton structures within the sample, thereby preparing it for subsequent liquid phase sintering.
Then, the liquid phase sintering was completed at the target sintering temperatures for 0.5 h, ensuring complete densification.

Finally, the temperature was rapidly decreased to 1420 ◦C to exit the liquid-phase sintering range, preventing excessive grain growth that could result from prolonged exposure to high-temperature liquid phases.

Macroscopically, the DL-PBF 98W samples exhibit only micro-crack defects (Fig. 2(a)). The double laser strategy ensures complete melting of W, thereby minimizing other potential defects.

At processing temperatures of 1350 ◦C + 1460 ◦C, the micro-crack defects within the sample are significantly reduced compared with the as-deposited sample (Fig. 2(c)). However, larger cracks persist due to the insufficient liquid phase formation, which hinders their complete healing.

mechanisms.name: crack self-healing by liquid phase backfilling

evidence.quote: At a temperature of 1500 ◦C, the low-melting-point Ni and Fe components melt to form a uniformly distributed liquid phase, which fully backfills micro-cracks within the DL-PBF 98W sample, enabling self-healing [19].
The transformation of W-grains morphologies is mainly due to the recrystallization of DL-PBF 98W sample during post-heat treatment.

in the liquid phase induced at 1500 ◦C, tungsten gradually spheroidizes and grows through the dissolution-precipitation mechanism (i.e., Ostwald ripening [21]), and the grain boundaries are rearranged.

At a temperature of 1500 ◦C, the low-melting-point Ni and Fe components melt to form a uniformly distributed liquid phase, which fully backfills micro-cracks within the DL-PBF 98W sample, enabling self-healing [19].
The transformation of W-grains morphologies is mainly due to the recrystallization of DL-PBF 98W sample during post-heat treatment.
the post-heat treatment (1350 ◦C + 1500 ◦C) effectively alleviated the residual stress, thereby reducing the average KAM value from 0.78◦ to 0.28◦ (Fig. 5(b2)).
For WHAs, the presence of γ matrix phase (Ni-Fe, W) could enhance the ductility and toughness of the samples [20].
Therefore, the heat treatment process of 1350 ◦C + 1500 ◦C was identified as the optimal regimen for DL-PBF 98 alloy.
